common_name: Prince Eugene Napoleon Camellia (Cherry-Red Formal Double Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or early spring into moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade; this old formal-double cultivar has circulated under several synonyms, so verify the source name matches the true cherry-red form before buying.

directions: Site this vigorous old camellia where afternoon shade shields the fully double, cherry-red blooms from fading and where the acidic, humus-rich soil it needs can be maintained with a heavy pine bark or pine straw mulch. Plants tolerate more sun in cooler climates but hold flower color and foliage quality best with morning sun and midday shelter in the Deep South. Because the name has been muddled with several synonymous selections over the decades, confirm nursery stock against a reliable regional camellia society reference before adding it to a collection. Water deeply during dry spells and prune lightly right after the late-winter to spring bloom to shape without sacrificing next year's buds.

common_name: Tomorrow's Dawn Camellia (White-Edged Pink Sport of 'Tomorrow')

planting.note: Plant container stock in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; Tomorrow's Dawn is a sport of 'Tomorrow' prized for its ruffled white-margined pink blooms and has itself produced further sports sold under related names.

directions: Give Tomorrow's Dawn a sheltered, partly shaded spot so its large, ruffled flowers keep their crisp white petal margins instead of bruising or browning in strong sun and wind. Like its parent cultivar 'Tomorrow', it grows into a dense, upright shrub and benefits from a thick acidic mulch layer to buffer soil moisture and temperature around the shallow root system. Thin out crowded interior growth after flowering to improve air circulation and reduce petal blight risk on the heavy double blooms. Because this cultivar occasionally reverts to solid pink or throws additional variegated sports, gardeners who want the true white-edged form should buy from a nursery that names its specific sport.
